subject: Renewal: provisioning additional reserved GPUs and on-demand fallback for NovaAI
messages:
From: Anne Kline <anne.k@novaai.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+contracts@novaai.com
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal review & capacity ask: reserved GPUs + overflow behavior

Hi Soojin,

Hope you’re doing well. Our annual renewal is approaching and traffic forecasts for Q3/Q4 show sustained growth — we expect baseline sustained throughput to rise ~2.5x and weekly production spikes that currently push us to ~3.8x baseline for short windows (10-30m).

We want to lock in additional reserved capacity for predictable latency and cost. Initial ask: +8 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (additive to our existing pool), with a throughput guarantee for our common inference fleet (target: 99th pct throughput guarantee, details below).

On overflow: we prefer not to hit a hard rejection during spikes. Two options we'd consider in the contract:
- Soft overflow: allow on-demand spillover to hosted capacity at a defined on-demand rate (billed) with clear throttles/alerts; or
- Hard cap: strict limit where extra requests are rejected once reserved capacity is saturated.

We prefer the soft overflow approach but need protection on cost spikes (monthly spend cap or automatic throttling after a budget threshold). I’ve attached a draft SOW (NovaAI_SOW_draft_v3.pdf) with our projected load curve and a short spreadsheet with expected percentiles.

Can your team propose a renewal addendum that includes reserved + overflow behavior options, and outline operational controls (alerts, canary rollouts, and billing caps)? Also please copy contracts so we can iterate on language.

Thanks,
Anne
Anne Kline
Head of ML Ops, NovaAI
ops+contracts@novaai.com

From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-05-03T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal review & capacity ask: reserved GPUs + overflow behavior

Hi Anne — thanks for the clear brief and the SOW. We can absolutely accommodate the request; below is a pragmatic set of options and the trade-offs so your procurement and ops teams can pick what they want in the renewal addendum.

Summary of options we recommend:
1) Reserved expansion + controlled on-demand fallback (recommended)
   - Add 8 reserved GPUs to your dedicated pool (same instance type you currently run).
   - Baseline guaranteed throughput: we’ll SLA 99th-pct throughput at your stated profile (we’ll formalize measurement windows in the SLO clause).
   - Soft overflow: when reserved capacity saturates, traffic routes to our hosted on-demand fleet. Overflow is allowed up to 50% of provisioned baseline capacity, billed at on-demand rates.
   - Safety throttle: if on-demand spend for overflow exceeds a monthly cushion (suggested initial cushion = $12k), the system will automatically drop to a protective mode where we gracefully degrade non-critical routes and send a manual approval request to your ops team.

2) Reserved expansion + hard cap (stricter, less cost exposure)
   - Add 8 reserved GPUs; any requests beyond reserved concurrency are rejected with a 429.
   - Good for predictable budgets; increases risk of request failures during spikes.

3) Hybrid canary ramp (recommended for first 30 days)
   - Start with option (1) but enable canary spillover on a per-route basis for 72-hour windows to validate latency/quality and billing impact.

Operational controls we’ll include in the addendum:
- Per-route overflow toggles (on/off) and per-route spend limits.
- 99th pct throughput reporting with token-level billing breakouts in Console.
- An automated alert (Slack + email + webhook) when on-demand overflow spend reaches 60% of the monthly cushion.
- A manual approval flow for auto-scale beyond twice the cushion in any 24h window.

Pricing delta rough estimate (pre-contracting): reserved monthly delta for +8 GPUs: $57,600/mo (committed rate). On-demand spillover billed at standard on-demand per-token rates; blended overage cap option available if you want spend smoothing. I’ll get formal numbers from Finance.

Next steps:
- Ben, can you confirm the technical safe overflow limit (routing + KV cache impacts) and an estimated latency delta for a 50% overflow?
- Dev, can you prepare a 7-step canary playbook we’ll attach as the rollout appendix?
- Anne, if this looks good we’ll draft a short addendum for contracts to review and add a DocuSign link for signature.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Exec, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai

Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal review & capacity ask: reserved GPUs + overflow behavior

Anne, Soojin — quick technical note to support the addendum drafting:

- Safe overflow sizing: based on NovaAI’s percentile sheet, a 50% on-demand overflow headroom maps to ~6-7 added A100-equivalent GPUs during peak windows. That will keep 95th pct tail latency within ~1.2x of reserved-only latency for typical token lengths.
- KV cache/latency: requests routed to hosted on-demand instances will not share your dedicated KV caches; cold starts cause a measurable initial latency bump for long chat sessions. Recommend enabling prefix caching on the client side and setting a 200ms spike-sla buffer in the SLO definition.
- Billing/guardrails: we can implement a soft spend cap that throttles background/low-priority routes first and leaves customer-facing routes on. We support webhook auto-approval flows so NovaAI can programmatically accept transient spend bursts above the cushion.

I’ve attached a short runbook with suggested thresholds and a canary checklist. For the contract we should specify the exact overflow multiplier (we used 50% above) and the monthly cushion in dollars or tokens.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal review & capacity ask: reserved GPUs + overflow behavior

Thanks, team — this is helpful. A few clarifications from NovaAI: 

1) We will accept the Reserved + Soft Overflow approach if two contract protections are in place:
   - A monthly on-demand spend cap tied to the renewal (we’d like an initial $10k cushion with an option to increase after 30 days), and
   - A 99th-pct throughput SLO measurement window and an explicit definition of what constitutes a violation (we prefer token-level measurements over per-request).

2) For billing smoothing: would Redwood consider a blended overage rate for overflow up to the cushion? That would help us avoid a jagged invoice when we have a single spike.

3) Can we get the canary playbook and a proposed 30-day ramp schedule in the addendum? We’ll route that to our legal/finance.

If you can model the projected impact on our renewal price (reserved delta + expected overflow blended costs assuming the percentile curve I sent), we’ll push this through our procurement fast-track.

Anne

Anne — glad we’re aligned. Summary / commitment we’ll include in the renewal addendum (short form):

1) Provisioning
   - Add 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs to NovaAI’s dedicated pool effective on renewal date.

2) Throughput SLA
   - 99th-pct throughput SLO measured at token-level over rolling 1-week windows; violations qualify for a service credit (text of credit TBD).

3) Overflow policy (final)
   - Soft overflow allowed up to 50% of provisioned baseline capacity (as Ben suggested).
   - On-demand overflow is billed at a blended overage rate for the first $10k of monthly overflow (we will propose a 15% discount on standard on-demand rates for that cushion).
   - If monthly overflow billing exceeds $10k, automated protective throttling will prioritize customer-facing routes and will send an approval request to ops+contracts@novaai.com. Any overflow beyond twice the cushion in a 24h window will require manual approval.

4) Canary & rollout
   - 7-day canary per-route, then 30-day ramp where overflow toggles are gradually opened. We’ll attach Ben’s runbook as Appendix A.

5) Docs/Signatures
   - I’ll route the addendum and the revised SOW to Contracts (cc: ops+contracts). Please review the DocuSign link once I post it; we’ll aim to lock pricing numbers in a single update.

If that meets NovaAI’s constraints I’ll draft the addendum and send the DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Soojin Lee

Redwood Inference
